Magic was chaos. Now it’s chemistry.

Through Stoichiomancy, power is measured, quantified, and controlled. Ascension follows a strict ladder, each tier with a fixed number of sanctioned seats.

There are no anomalies.

Until Arielle Blacksoil.

Born to a bloodline without magic, Arielle should have been invisible to the system. Instead, an accident reveals the impossible:

She’s an unsanctioned archmage.

If discovered, they’ll strip her power or turn her into a weapon.

To survive, Arielle enrolls in the Academy and pretends to climb the ranks while hiding magic that eclipses her professors.

For the first time in her life, she has rivals, teammates…maybe even friends. 

But hiding overwhelming power isn’t easy.

Pretty soon, she’s embroiled in faction conflict, foiling villainous plots and hunting a mysterious primordial that lurks in the dark.

Sinope Ananke should be dead.

Sin just escaped a nightmare posting aboard the massive Leviathan-class transport ship Mimir with nothing but the clothes on her back and a desperate plan.

She made it offship and to the nearest orbital station with no one the wiser—except for the orbital station officials who just threw her into their brig, having found her passed out by an unsecured airlock, apparently about to jump into the void without a suit.

Now she’s been rescued by Captain Jack Grace of the independent courier ship Cassanda, a fast-packet hauler trying to break into the lucrative cryogenic cargo business. Grace needs someone with a rare skillset: a Bot Driver capable of running a swarm of specialized robots that maintain fragile cargo in transit.

Sin needs to get out of the sector before the people she ran from realize she’s still alive.

Two problems. One convenient solution. Right?

There’s just one complication.

Sin carries the Black Spot, a mark spacers swear draws the attention of something hungry in the dark between stars—something that eats ships.

Grace thinks that’s just superstition.

Sin isn’t so sure. After all, she's already experienced the impossible once.

She hadn’t been trying to get out of that airlock.

She had just gotten in.

What to Expect:

- Mystery! How did Sin survive the vacuum of space and what is the Black Spot, really?

- Adventure! How many problems can one tramp freighter ship encounter? More than you would think!

- Queers in Spaaaaace (wlw, mlm)

- Seven huge personalities sharing one small space ship

- Space Opera Level Human Diaspora

- Transhumanism

Launching on July 1, 2026

Sin & Grace will be start with 5 chapters at launch and update daily until 7/10, and then 2x a week on Tuesdays and Thursdays. 

Patrons will be able to read up to FIVE CHAPTERS ahead of Royal Road.

Orange-crest is a monkey with simple desires. He likes warm summer days lazing about with his brothers and sisters, sampling the variety of fruit and grubs Mount Yuelu provides its simian inhabitants. He does not like tigers, or that one green fruit that makes one's shits white and runny. Unlike his brothers though, orange-crest is endlessly curious. And no subject arouses that curiosity more than the many mysteries of fermentation. One fateful night, he finds himself enjoying an experimental brew a little more potent than his usual work.

Daoist Scouring Medicine is a man disgraced. Caught between the pressures of a vision for pill refining he will not compromise, and the politics of a world that discards its ideals the moment they stand in the way of profit; his once rising star has long since stagnated. After a disciple from a prestigious and wealthy family cripples himself by misusing the daoist's work, he finds himself wandering the slopes of an unfamiliar mountain, hitting the gourd a little harder than any self-respecting daoist should, cursing the Heavens and the Zhang family alike.

From a pair of poorly considered drunken decisions, a sequence of events are set into motion that will one day shake the very heavens.

Updates once a week on Wednesdays.

There is no Epic Loot here, Only Puns.

The Holy Empire is in decline.

Religious and cultural schisms wreak havoc on its internal politics, while revolutions are brewing in neighboring kingdoms. The aristocratic houses play endless power games amongst themselves, and the Emperor desperately abuses what little influence he has left to keep his rivals down.

Amidst all of this, Arnold von Hohenfels, first son of the Margrave of Hohenfels, finds himself in the unfortunate position of having to attend the Imperial Academy, a notorious battleground of wits and brawn for ambitious young nobles.

Armed with a magical gift that is as much a blessing as it is a curse, he must learn to navigate the treacherous waters of aristocratic entanglements. In the name of his family’s ambition, he must represent House Hohenfels' interests in this microcosm of Imperial politics, deal with his formidable enemies, form alliances of his own, and somehow keep his brash cousin Friedrich out of trouble.

Frankly, he would much rather be anywhere else.

Once upon a time, on a certain dark planet called Surcease live the Kaedekin. 

Clones of a single magical girl, the Kaedekin have spent the last several hundred years building up from a single crashed ship and three thousand survivors into a planet-spanning civilization. It's been difficult. The life native to the planet is inedible, the heavy metal content of everything makes everything very complicated, the perpetual darkness blocking out the visible light of the nearby star makes everything very complicated, and the random kaiju created by the mutagenic void energies coming from certain spots on the planet make everything very... you get the idea. 

Oh, and every year the chance that they'll finally make first contact with one of the many space-faring polities in that galaxy that they've been listening to increases. 

That year has finally come.

Mark Castle loves horror movies. But when he died in the hands of a cult, he is reincarnated and forced to become a dungeon core…

And makes his domain as a lonely cabin in the woods. With newfound powers, he starts his revenge on the people who murdered him.

Utilizing all the tropes and monster manuals of his favorite horror books and movies, Mark sets up a simple rule: lure unwitting victims into the cabin, kill them off one by one, and feed his core with their souls. If anyone is lucky enough to survive until dawn, he rewards them with treasure...and their lives.

But as Mark feeds and grows, the people who hunger for his unique power begin to take notice, and Mark is in even more danger than he imagined.

The Cabin is Always Hungry is a dungeon-core horror slasher and progression LitRPG with brutal deaths, dozens of horror movie-inspired monsters, classic horror settings, and plenty of redshirts.

Fair Warning: Mind the Violence and Gore tag. They are there for a reason.

Book 3 (Arc 5) - ONGOING

The Voice gave Mark a second life and sent him to a world where people like him are burned at the stake. It just forgot to explain what the priests would be looking for.

Mark had already survived the worst years of his life. Then he wasted the ones that came after them. He had plans. Good ones, even. He just never got around to starting them.

Instead of waking up as a legendary hero, however, he finds himself trapped in the body of a nameless infant in a dirt-poor farming family.

To claim this second life, Mark must survive the temple's tests and prove he isn't Abyss-touched. 

All he has is the promise of a System that refuses to fully awaken, and a Trait hidden behind a blacked-out name.

No powerful mentor waiting to guide him. No legendary artifact falling into his lap. No power without effort.

In a world shaped by Traits, Professions, and power, most people spend their lives trying to become someone.

Mark's problem is figuring out what he already is.

A character-driven slow-burn progression fantasy about second chances, family, mystery, and power earned one step at a time.

Three books and 140+ chapters already written.

As the perfect sacrifice, it is only natural that Nix be sacrificed to the ancient gods lurking in the depths of the black hole.

But she didn’t die.

Finding herself seven years in the past — to the day of her first cursed mutation — Nix is determined to correct her regrets, enact vengeance on her murderers, and simply live the life that she never got to. But even with this second chance, freedom from the cults remains a pipe dream. To achieve everything she never could in her previous life, there is only one path before her.

Lysanthia, the strongest Demon Queen, spent centuries trying to die.

Not because she wanted death. It was the only way to break her chains.

Her reincarnation spell worked -mostly. She woke in a forest nearly a thousand years in the future, in a body that wasn't quite hers, stripped of her overwhelming power. A world without a System. Without Classes. Without the Gods watching her every step.

Her reincarnation is complicated by the presence of Ash, the Hero who slew her. She's now thrust into a world almost completely alien, yet somehow recognizable -a world where power is etched in Ink, and where she must start from nothing.

A world where some people show her kindness for no reason at all. That might be harder than starting over.

For the first time in eons, the strongest Demon Queen is free. Not even she knows what comes next.

What to expect:

- A once very overpowered FMC, now forced to get overpowered all over again. Though, not every problem can be solved by punching (and some are caused by punching).

- A Demon Queen learning to be more than what she was.

- Power system (cultivation adjacent) introduced in chapter 9. Be patient.

- Arcs that are slower paced, arcs more focused around faster power progression/action.
